cands.bio: Republican candidate for California's 3rd Congressional District in 2026. Former President/CEO of a family-owned mobilehome community business, which was sold in 2020. Elected to the Nevada County Board of Supervisors in 2024. Holds a Pepperdine business degree and a Wheaton College Graduate School master's.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed by Ballotpedia, along with several online voter guides)

cands.gaps: The platform page we could read was cut off partway through, so we have none of his stated positions on guns, abortion, schools, immigration, housing and land use, data centers, or property taxes. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no documented statement from him on data centers or development limits beyond a general line about a balance of growth, development and agriculture. We did not find his county board votes in official records; his campaign site describes them, but a campaign site is not a record of what he did. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in the pages we had. Local news coverage of his time as a supervisor was not available.

cands.bio: Physician and Democratic U.S. House member from the Sacramento area since 2013. Former Sacramento County chief medical officer and UC Davis clinical professor. Won election in 2026 in California's redrawn 3rd District after representing districts 7 and 6.

controversies.text: Federal records show $7,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate.
Missed 10 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (1.5%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 4, 2025-02-06 to 2025-02-07.

endorsements.text: Planned Parenthood Action Fund, as cited on his campaign site

cands.gaps: We found no documented stance from Bera on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas, police pay and pensions, gun laws, or school vouchers and charters. The Ballotpedia page we read was cut off partway through its list of key votes, so earlier-session votes were not readable. Bera did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. His birthplace and upbringing come from Wikipedia alone; no primary record was available.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.
